descripcion_geo: Fertile plateau northeast of Lake Galilee and east of the Jordan, famous for its bulls and oaks.
importancia_estrategica: Agricultural and livestock region disputed between Israel and the Aramean kingdoms.

historias.titulo: Victory over King Og by Bashan
historias.descripcion: Israel defeats the giant Og, king of Bashan, in Edrei; His iron bed was nine cubits long.

historias.titulo: The bulls of Bashan in Psalm 22
historias.descripcion: Psalm 22 uses the 'bulls of Bashan' as a metaphor for the enemies that surround the righteous sufferer.

historias.titulo: The Transfiguration on Hermon by Bashan
historias.descripcion: Mount Hermon, on the borders of Bashan, is the probable location of the Transfiguration of Jesus.

personajes.descripcion: Last of the Rephaim; His defeat allowed Israel to control the northern Transjordan.
He conquered the villages of Bashan called 'the villages of Yair'.
He traveled through the territories near Bashan in his escapes and pilgrimages.

contexto_religioso.contexto_lugar: Land of giants, exuberant livestock and sacred oaks; His biblical images range from threat (bulls) to abundance.

judaismo.descripcion: The bulls of Bashan were the largest and fiercest in the ancient world; Psalm 22 uses them as an image of the enemies of the righteous.
judaismo.significado_teologico: The bulls of Bashan were the largest and fiercest in the ancient world; Psalm 22 uses them as an image of the enemies of the righteous.

cristianismo.fuente_primaria: Nuevo Testamento / Padres de la Iglesia
cristianismo.descripcion: The Church Fathers interpreted the 'bulls of Bashan' of Psalm 22 as a prefiguration of the persecutors of Christ.
cristianismo.significado_teologico: The Church Fathers interpreted the 'bulls of Bashan' of Psalm 22 as a prefiguration of the persecutors of Christ.
